answer: Shale-Inlet Lottery Quotas.** Each epoch, a verifiable random function seeded by a public beacon assigns agents to shards; only the drawn shard may submit work, and assignment slots are capped per seed. An attacker cannot precompute which identities will land where, so flooding requires buying slots across many independent draws. Excess identities wander across unselected shards, earning nothing. The per-identity cost is the wasted registration and idle capacity for each lottery loss.
